svg.aria-label: The same neighbors can give different KNN votes Panel: Distances from the query Panel: Compare the vote totals The same $k = 3$ neighbors Feature x: -4 to 3 Feature y: -2 to 5 Class A (scatter): a1 A1 (0, 2); a2 A2 (-3, 0) Class B (scatter): b1 B1 (1, 0) Query q (scatter): q q (0, 0) A1: $d = 2$; $1/d = \frac{1}{2}$: (0, 0) → (0, 2) A2: $d = 3$; $1/d = \frac{1}{3}$: (0, 0) → (-3, 0) B1: $d = 1$; $1/d = 1$: (0, 0) → (1, 0) Euclidean distance from $q = (0, 0)$. All three training points vote; none has zero distance. Count neighbors or sum inverse distances Dist. | Uniform vote | $1/d$ vote A1 (Class A): 2 | 1 | $\frac{1}{2}$ A2 (Class A): 3 | 1 | $\frac{1}{3}$ B1 (Class B): 1 | 1 | 1 Class A total: — | 2 | $\frac{5}{6}$ Class B total: — | 1 | 1 Winner: — | A | B Winner: highlighted row Uniform voting gives A two votes. Inverse-distance voting gives B more weight: $1 > \frac{5}{6}$. At $k = 3$, uniform voting predicts A; weights $w = 1/d$ predict B. The closer B neighbor outweighs the two A neighbors.
